questions.question: How are sounds made? Give two examples.
questions.expected_answer: Sounds are made when something vibrates, which means it moves quickly backwards and forwards. For example, vocal cords vibrate when we hum, a guitar string vibrates when plucked, a drum skin vibrates when hit, or a ruler vibrates when twanged on a desk.

questions.question: Describe how sound travels from a drum to your ear.
questions.expected_answer: The vibrating drum skin pushes on the air next to it, and the vibration is passed from one bit of air to the next, spreading outwards in all directions. When it reaches your ear, it makes your eardrum vibrate, and your brain turns this into the sound you hear.

questions.question: Name four materials that sound can travel through, and one place where it cannot travel.
questions.expected_answer: Sound can travel through air, water, wood, plastic and metal. It cannot travel through empty space, where there is no material, for example in space or on the Moon, which has no air.
